# Continual-ARC learned patterns

## Reflected triptych / diptych tiling — task-0d669ea9 (verified correct)
For an H×W grid, make a 3H×2W output. Row ordering is vertically flipped source rows, then original source rows, then vertically flipped source rows. Each row consists of the horizontally reversed source row followed by the unchanged source row. Thus output rows are generated by `reverse(row) + row` for source row sequence `reversed(rows) + rows + reversed(rows)`. Verified on a 5×13 demonstration → 15×26 output and an 8×7 test → 24×14 accepted output. Do not use simple tiling; preserve this particular flip/order arrangement.

## Tiled-room corner markers

## Rule inferred from task-1377fd69 (verified correct)

The input is a large regularly tiled grid: thick/background wall lines form rectangular rooms, and most room interiors share a single background color. Some wall-line intersections are recolored. Decode to a smaller room grid:

1. Locate the repeating horizontal and vertical wall lines (the line rows/columns are usually easy to spot because nearly all cells on them share a wall color). Determine the complete rectangles/rooms bounded by consecutive wall lines. Ignore partial rooms clipped by the outside edge of the input; include only rectangles with all four line intersections inside the grid.
2. The output has one cell per such complete room, in the same top-to-bottom, left-to-right order.
3. Initialize each output cell to the common room-interior color.
4. For each room, inspect the four intersections of its two bounding horizontal lines with its two bounding vertical lines. If all four corners have the same non-wall/special color, use that color for the corresponding output cell. Otherwise leave the room-interior color.

This is a 2x2 corner-consensus rule, not a sampling of one corner and not a direct copy of the special intersections. In the demonstration, 27x23 input had wall-line rows 1,4,...,25 and columns 1,8,15,22. Edge-clipped partial rooms were omitted, yielding a 6x3 output with base color 8; a 5 or 2 was placed where all four room corners shared that color. In the test, complete rooms were bounded by rows 0,5,10,15,20 and columns 0,6,12,18,24, yielding 4x4 output with base color 2. The verified answer was:

[[2,2,2,7],
 [6,2,2,2],
 [2,2,2,2],
 [2,1,2,8]]

## Caution

Do not infer output size solely from all repeated wall lines: remove edge-clipped incomplete rooms. A single marked corner or only two matching corners does not suffice; require all four corners of a room to agree on the same special color. Avoid spending demo requests unless an example genuinely distinguishes competing rules.
